questions.student_answer:
Have you every wondered how monarch butterflies are able to survive winter?




Every fall, millions of monarch butterflies fly thousands of miles down south to Mexico in order to survive winter. Once in Mexico, they spend the winter resting in trees. When spring comes, new generations of monarch butterflies fly north again, stopping to eat and lay eggs along the way.




In recent years, fewer butterflies have completed this journey due to humans clearing forests and farmland. This has destroyed milkweed which is monarchs main source of food. Strong storms have also damaged the forests where monarchs spend the winter in.




In order to help, people become citizen scientists.They tag butterflies and record where they travel in order to help scientists track migration patterns.




In conclusion, although monarch butterfly populations continue to dwindle, citzen scientists are stepping up in order to save these beautiful creatures. So the next time you see a monarch butterfly, think about what you can do to help it out.

questions.student_answer:
Sleep is one of the most important tasks your body does, because it helps your brain clean itself and it helps you remember what you learned.

Your brain has a special cleaning system that works best while you sleep. This system, called the glymphatic system, washes away harmful waste products that build up during the day. Think of it like a dishwasher for your brain! The cleaning happens when brain cells shrink and create more space for fluid to flow through. This process helps protect your brain from diseases and keeps it working properly.

Sleep also plays a huge role in helping you remember what you learned during the day. While you sleep, your brain moves important memories from short-term storage to long-term storage. Students who get enough sleep perform better on tests than those who stay up late. Additionally, sleep helps your brain make connections between different ideas and solve more easily.

Most kids your age need about nine to eleven hours of sleep each night to stay healthy. Unfortunately, many students don't get enough sleep because of homework, after school activties, or screen time. When you don't sleep enough, you might feel grumpy, have trouble pay attention, or get sick more often. You rimmune system becomes weaker without proper rest.

In conclusion, sleep is very important for kids if they want to do well in school.

Use information from the passage to support your explanation. write an expository essay Make sure your response includes the following: Introduction with a strong thesis, 3 body paragraphs with topic sentences, and a conclusion (5 points) Write 5 clear paragraphs: Support each point with facts or examples from the passage and explain what they show
incorrect_questions.student_answer:
Sleep is one of the most important tasks your body does, because it helps your brain clean itself and it helps you remember what you learned.

Your brain has a special cleaning system that works best while you sleep. This system, called the glymphatic system, washes away harmful waste products that build up during the day. Think of it like a dishwasher for your brain! The cleaning happens when brain cells shrink and create more space for fluid to flow through. This process helps protect your brain from diseases and keeps it working properly.

Sleep also plays a huge role in helping you remember what you learned during the day. While you sleep, your brain moves important memories from short-term storage to long-term storage. Students who get enough sleep perform better on tests than those who stay up late. Additionally, sleep helps your brain make connections between different ideas and solve more easily.

Most kids your age need about nine to eleven hours of sleep each night to stay healthy. Unfortunately, many students don't get enough sleep because of homework, after school activties, or screen time. When you don't sleep enough, you might feel grumpy, have trouble pay attention, or get sick more often. You rimmune system becomes weaker without proper rest.

In conclusion, sleep is very important for kids if they want to do well in school.

questions.prompt: Write an  explaining how people are helping monarch butterflies survive. expository essay  Use information from the passage to support your ideas.   : Make sure your response includes the following  : Introduction with a strong thesis, 3 body paragraphs with topic sentences, and a conclusion (5 points) Write 5 clear paragraphs   : Support each point with facts or examples from the passage and explain what they show (5 points) Use evidence and explain it   : Use transitions, keep your ideas in or
questions.student_answer:
For Carter's ninth birthday, he didn't want games or anything like that. Instead, he wanted to donations to help monarch butterflies. Carter wanted to build a station-a small garden where monarchs could rest and lay eggs. With some parent help, he was able to clear part of his bakyard in Virginia and plant rows of milyweed, the butterflies' favorite food. After that, he waited for them to come.




Every fall, thousands of monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles from Canada all the way down to Mexico. There, they spend their time in trees until spring comes around. When spring finally arrives, they fly back north and lay eggs and eat along their journey back. This is one of the most remarkable migrations in nature.




Sadly, in the recent years, fewer butterflies have been able to complete this migration. Humans have created farms and cities that have destroyed milkweed plants that these butterflies depend on. Humans aren't the only reasons that milkweed plants are getting destroyed, storms have also taken a big role in this by destroying forests in which they would spend their winter in. Scientists worry that the number of these butterflies is shrinking. 




To help, thousands of people across North America have become citizen scientists. They tag butterflies with small stickers, count caterpillers, and post these monarch sightings online. These reports help scientists know how these butterflies are doing and where they need protection. 




Carter continues to raise and tag monarchs in his yard. He believes that even the smallest actions can make a very big impact. "Humans may be the problem," he says, "but we are also the solution to help these animals." Thanks to helpers like Carter and anyone who volunteers to help, monarchs may have a higher chance to survive.

questions.student_answer:
In a neighboorhood café, many people speak different languages. A family speaks Spanish, a worker is singing in French song on the radio.These scenes happen all over the United States, a country shaoed by immigrants. Even though English is the most common language spoken at school, many young children speak two languages at home and at school.




Learning a second language helps people in many ways. Studies show that learning a second language can improve memory and prolem-solving skills. Scientists say that it is easy for young children to learn new sounds since their brains are developing. This means that young children have strong head start when learning a new language. 




One way children learn a new language is through immersion. In an immersion class, the classe's teacher uses the new language throughout the entire school day. Students hear the new language during class lessons, group work, and even simple request like asking to use the restroom. Since they have to use the new language all day, they start picking it up. They even learn grammar by listening to how it is used in real life. 




Another useful method schools use is cumminication. Some claasrooms connect students with pen pals from other countries around the globe. Children write letters or emails on their computer and share stories about them and their daily lives. These friendships help motivate students to to practice new languages more and help understand different cultures. Real communication shows that language learning has a useful purpose.




Experts still study how peoples' age affects the language learning. Some experts believe that older students have an easier time learning in structured classrooms. Other experts believe that younger students naturally learn because they mimic sounds and accents more easily No matter what the method is, language learning can open doors. It helps kids connect with other and explore the world with confidence.

questions.student_answer:
For many years, the Mithi River in Mumbai, India, was full of trash. Factories dumped waste into the water. Sewage flowed in every day. The river turned black, and it smelled so bad that people stayed away.

Then a group called Earth5R decided to help. They wanted to clean up the river and make it healthy again. They knew it would take time and hard work. They also knew they could not do it alone.

First, the group mapped out the dirtiest parts of the river. They tested the river to see where the problems were the worst. Then they held cleanup events and asked people to help out. They invited families, schools, and local shops and business. At first, few poeple came. But soon, more and more joined. After a few months, the group had collected over fourteen tonnes of trash. 

Next, Earth5R worked with scientists to plant grasses along the banks of the river. These plants help clean the river and stop the soil from washing away. The group also sorted the trash they found. They recycled plasicts and turned food scraps into compost. 

Over time, the river began to look and smell better. Tests showed the water was 20% cleaner than before. People started to visit the bank again. 

The project taught the community a lot. Many people said they had ignored the river for many years. They thought someone else would fix it. Now they saw that change starts when regular people take action. Business who doubted the project at first beame big supporters. Volunteers learned that small actions add up over time. Have you ever wondered what it is liek to live in space? 

On the ISS, astronauts follow routines that keep them healthy and not messy. 

The ISS circles Earth every ninety minutes, so the crew use Coordinated Univaresal Time so that everyone is able to stay on the same schedule while in space. 




In the morning, astronauts do simple tasks sich as taking showers and brushing their teeth, but it can be very challenging since they are in space. Manu things can happend such as water floating in small drops, swallowing toothpaste, and loose items drifting. Breakfast can be very quick because the worday is busy. A lot of foods are de-hydrated or heat stabilized, so the astronauts add warm or hot water to re-hydrate some foods.  More ways are used to make sure that things dont float away such as foods that stay together and meal pouches that can attatch to trays.




A very big oart of each and everday is spent on scientific reaserch. The ISS has a microgravity environment that lets scientists work how plants gtow and other scientific things. All of the experiments have to be set up very carefully. Tings such as wires, tubes, and others are secured so they do not drift around the cabin. 




Exercise is also a very important part of being in space. If they did not have gravity, there muscles and bones would weaken fast.  The astronauts work for two hours a day, using equipment such as a harness, a bycical, and a resistece devise. These activites assist the crew to stay strong. The evenings can be calmer, so they do small tasks, talk with mission control, and eat food. Right before bed, each astronuat goes into a small sleeping bag that is attatched to a wall so they do nto float around.




Even though the life on the ISS is very different form the life we have on earth, the astronauts do routines and stay safe. With careful planning and teamowrk, they can do many things in space.

questions.title: Extended Text Question
questions.student_answer:
Have you ever wondered how memories are made? You should think about your first day of school, and everything that made you feel nervous. How might the brain keep that experience? The answer includes a thing that sceintists are still trying to figure out.

Each and every memory starts with an expeirience, such as when something happens, the senses can collecy information and then they send electrical signals to your brain. The signals can move on the pathways that are made out of nerve cells called neurons. The brain of a human has rouhgly eight-six billion neurons. When two neurons meet, a small gap call a synapse causes the signal to go through one cell to a nother. The stronger it is, the stonger the signal. This stage is called encoding.

Not all of the experiences becomes a long lasting memory. Short memories holds information for about 30 seconds. To move into long term storage, the memory must be consolidated. This is where the hippocampus can play a important role. It sort of acts similar to a sorting center, which decides what it wants to keep. While people sleep, the hippocampus replays the events that happened in the day and helps strenghten neural connections. Some studies have found that people who sleep good after studying keep in up to 40 percent more information than those who stay up the entire night.

Getting your memory back is not similer to opening a file on your computer. The brain reconstructs the memory by activating it again. This means that memories can be changed a little but each time. The mood you have, the surroundings, and conversations you had. recently can influence the outcome of how good you remember things. In a experiment held in 1975, there were divers who memorized words underwater and remember them better when they were tested again underwater and not onland. Some scientists call this state-dependent memory.

Forgetting things is not a flaw always, so by letting go of details you dont need, your brain can be efficient and can focus on what matters most. But without forgetting things, old informations could interfere with new information.

questions.prompt: Based on the passage 'The Invention of Writing,' . Use information from the passage to support your ideas. write an expository essay explaining how the invention of writing changed the way people recorded and shared knowledge Organise your ideas clearly and support them with details from the text. Make sure your response includes the following: : Introduction with a strong thesis, 3 body paragraphs with topic sentences, and a conclusion (5 points) Write 5 clear paragraphs : Support each point wi
questions.student_answer:
Did you know that for most of history, the people of the world passed information on only by speaking. Many things survivded only by those who heard them, meaning that no knowledge could be saved by being written down. Being able to write change all of this in many ways.

The writing system that is the oldest known began around 3400 BCE in a plasce called Mesopotomia, which is a region between two different rivers in what is now Iraq. The sumerians pressed wedge shaped marks into a piece of soft clay tablets. Scholars call this cuneiform. In the start, these marks stood for real things like grain and cattle; over time, the marks changed to stand for other things like sounds.

At about the same time, the Egyptians developed hieroglyphics, which is a system that combined pictures with some sound symbols. Different from cuneiform, hieroglyphics were often carved into stone or painted on scrolls. Scribes can only copy important texts and send them to temples and officials in far-away cities, which spread the knowledge. These two systems took many yeard to learn and understand,and because on few people like trained scribes could read and write, they had lots of power in their governments.

Being able to write changed the way people lived in many ways. Some traders could keep trfack of the deals made across distances. Rulers were able to pass written laws that applied to all people. Something call the Code of Hammurabi, which was on of the oldest set of laws, had almost tree hundered rules whch helped the daily lives of the people. Many thinkers could build on the work on those people that came before them without starting a new stage.

It is very interesting to think about how our daily lives would be different if nobody had ever pressed a pen into clay. These days, billions of people can reead and write each day, but what began on clay tablets became the start of science and many others things.
